Faculty of Science and Engineering - School of Architecture, Computing and Engineering

Fixed Term: 36-month contract

Full time: 37 Hours per week

The University of Wolverhampton is seeking an exceptional MSc or PhD graduate to join a pioneering Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) with Korutek Engineering Ltd, one of the UK's leading low carbon food cooling solutions providers.

As a surface engineer (KTP Associate) you will develop and help commercialise MuMiGroovEs (Multiscale MicroGrooves) evaporators, a passive, ultra-efficient anti-frost fin technology that keeps freezers running. You will be employed by the University of Wolverhampton and work full-time to the company's Norwich premises for the 36-month project duration.

 Co-funded by Innovate UK and Korutek Engineering Ltd, this KTP brings together world-class academic expertise in coalescence-induced jumping-droplet condensation and superhydrophobic micro-grooved surfaces with Korutek's deep industry knowledge. The partnership will deliver commercially viable anti-frost fin packs, enabling a step-change in energy efficiency, frost reduction and system compactness.

 Main Duties and Responsibilities include:

Technical Development

Develop multiscale micro-grooved surface engineering, laser micromachining of aluminium and advanced thermo-fluids protocols specifically for Korutek Engineering.
Develop a highly efficient, scalable and sustainable evaporator technology that cuts energy use, reduces defrosting, boosts productivity and lowers environmental impact for freezing and chilling systems
Develop in-house capability in surface engineering and laser-texturing, delivering major energy savings, cut frost accumulation, extend production time, and allow retrofit installation
Design, optimise and test laser-etched micro-grooves, from nano- to micro-scale, that trigger coalescence-induced jumping-droplet shedding so condensate leaves the fin before it can freeze.
A dedicated test freezer will benchmark performance over six months of freeze-thaw trial
Remove the need to use fluoropolymer coatings which carry PFAS forever chemicals

Research, Innovation and Commercialisation

Apply state-of-the-art research in multiscale micro-grooved surface engineering, laser micromachining of aluminium and advanced thermo-fluids to practical use cases.
Engage with academic experts to ensure the scientific validity and robustness of the solution.
Contribute to academic publications, industry-focused project demonstrators, and knowledge dissemination.
Support the company in creating a sustainable model for MuMiGroovEs within the business.
Engage regularly with scoping and estimating, design and commercial team and other stakeholders to refine product-market fit and user experience
Contribute to intellectual property development and the exploration of commercial pathways for MuMiGroovEs

 Project Management and Stakeholder Engagement

Plan, monitor, and deliver KTP project milestones on time and within scope.
Produce progress reports and presentations for senior stakeholders and Innovate UK.
Work collaboratively across academic and industrial teams. 

 What we are looking for

MSc or PhD in Mechanical Engineering or Project Management. 
A background in Surface Engineering/Modifications and/or Thermofluids
Competency in control systems and automation
Design and fabrication experience is highly desirable
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an entrepreneurial mindset.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills including the ability to engage effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

This role offers a competitive salary alongside a dedicated personal training and development budget to invest in building your skills across the life of the project. You will also have the opportunity to attend the fully funded KTP residential leadership and management programme facilitated by Innovate UK. Working closely with leading researchers at the University of Wolverhampton, you will have the opportunity to contribute to academic publications and develop a credible research profile that runs alongside your industry delivery.

There will be the opportunity to interact with company staff, industrial partners, clients as well as University of Wolverhampton academics. The role will allow the successful candidate to apply their knowledge to a commercial project, finding creative innovative solutions to industry problems. For an informal discussion about the post please contact Professor Arun Arjunan at the University of Wolverhampton (A.Arjunan@wlv.ac.uk)

About Us

We seek to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Toxicology to join the team of Dr Luigi Margiotta-Casaluci at the  Institute of Pharmaceutical Science, King's College London, in collaboration with Professor Christer Hogstrand.

The Margiotta-Casaluci lab specialises in mechanistic and translational toxicology, developing next-generation predictive methods — including AI-driven approaches, Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) frameworks, and advanced zebrafish and human in vitro models — to decode the adverse effects of chemicals and their mixtures. The post is part of HARMONY (Hazard Assessment of Marine Mixtures and New Pollutant Synergies), a €10M Horizon Europe-funded international research programme investigating the cumulative impacts of marine pollutants on ecosystems and human health, through a One Health lens. At King's, we lead the AI and computational modelling work, developing next-generation predictive tools for mixture toxicity assessment in collaboration with a multidisciplinary consortium of 15 partners across Europe and India. We foster a collaborative and inclusive research culture, with access to state-of-the-art facilities including the King's Institute for Artificial Intelligence, the Hub of Applied Bioinformatics, and high-performance computng platforms. We are committed to supporting the career development of our researchers and to producing internationally impactful science at the interface of toxicology, data science, and environmental health policy.

 https://www.kcl.ac.uk/people/luigi-margiotta-casaluci

 https://www.margiotta-casaluci-lab.com

About The Role

Marine ecosystems are increasingly threatened by complex mixtures of chemical pollutants — including pharmaceuticals, PFAS, microplastics, and heavy metals — whose cumulative impacts on wildlife and human health remain poorly understood. Current risk assessment frameworks are largely designed for individual chemicals and fail to capture the synergistic, additive, or antagonistic effects that emerge from real-world mixture exposures. Addressing this challenge requires a fundamental shift toward mechanistically informed, AI-powered predictive approaches.

We are seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Toxicology to lead the AI and predictive modelling activities of the HARMONY project at King's College London. The successful candidate will develop and apply cutting-edge computational tools to predict the toxicity and biological effects of complex pollutant mixtures in marine organisms, with implications for both environmental and human health. This will include the development of AI and machine learning models — including graph neural networks, geometric deep learning, mode-of-action-informed QSARs, Bayesian networks, and multi-agent AI frameworks — trained on multi-omics, chemical, and biological datasets generated across the HARMONY consortium. The candidate will also apply cheminformatics approaches for chemical grouping and toxicity driver identification, develop and apply Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks, and use concentration addition and independent action models to assess cumulative mixture effects across species. There will also be opportunities to explore the application of large language models (LLMs) and agentic AI systems for data extraction, probabilistic risk assessment, and science-to-policy translation.

The post is part of HARMONY (Hazard Assessment of Marine Mixtures and New Pollutant Synergies), a Horizon Europe-funded international research programme involving 15 partners across Europe and India. The successful candidate will play a central role in delivering the AI-enabled predictive toxicology components of the project, coordinating modelling activities with consortium partners and contributing to the project's policy-relevant outputs. The role involves close collaboration with experimental teams generating zebrafish, in vitro, and field data across the consortium, translating complex biological datasets into regulatory-ready predictive frameworks.

The candidate will contribute to high-impact scientific publications, present at national and international conferences, assist with grant reporting, and will have the opportunity to co-supervise PhD and MSc students. The successful candidate will also be supported to develop their independent research profile and apply for postdoctoral fellowship.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed-term contract up until 31 Aug 2029.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

PhD in a relevant discipline (computational toxicology, cheminformatics, data science, bioinformatics, or related field).
Demonstrated experience in developing and applying AI/ML models for toxicological, biomedical, or environmental applications.
Proficiency in Python and relevant scientific libraries (e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow, RDKit, scikit-learn).
Strong quantitative and statistical skills, including Bayesian approaches.
Evidence of scientific publication or manuscript preparation.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multi-partner projects.

Desirable criteria

Experience with multi-level data integration.
Experience with QSAR modelling and cheminformatics approaches for chemical property or toxicity predictions.
Knowledge of environmental or regulatory toxicology frameworks (e.g. EFSA, FSA, ECHA, REACH).
Experience with large language models (LLMs) or multi-agent AI systems.
Familiarity with Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) development and AOP network modelling.

We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.  

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.  

The role

The Institute for Communication Systems (ICS) home of the 5G and 6G Innovation Centre (5GIC/6GIC) is looking to recruit a Research Fellow in Neuromorphic and Quantum-Inspired Computing: Foundations and Applications in Wireless Communications. The successful candidate will be part of the Wireless Systems Lab group and will have the opportunity to work very close with our industrial partners as well as with academic partners all over the world.

The post is part of a major EU-funded 6G research project in which the University of Surrey leads the work on cross-layer co-design of RAN workloads for emerging-computing accelerators. The project investigates how next-generation radio access networks can be made radically more energy-efficient by moving computationally intensive physical-layer (PHY) functions away from conventional digital hardware and onto emerging computing architectures. These include neuromorphic (spiking and event-driven), in-memory and analogue computing.

The post holder will undertake research in neuromorphic, in-memory and other unconventional computing architectures for future wireless communication systems. The research will focus on physical-layer receiver processing and on architectures that reduce reliance on high-resolution analogue-to-digital conversion and conventional digital 

ICS is the largest academic research institute in Europe specialising in all aspects of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies). It is home to over 200 researchers with expertise in all communication and broadcasting systems and has developed the best in class large scale testbeds for research and innovation and enjoys the state-of-the-art lab and computing facilities.

Established in 2012, 5GIC is the world’s first dedicated centre in researching end-to-end aspects of 5G and works closely with national and international leading academic institutes and key industrial partners. In November 2020, 6GIC was officially launched with parallel research undertaken in both 5G+ and 6G for 2030+.

Please refer to the essential criteria in the Job Profiles for a Research Fellow A and B attached for further details.

3) Interpersonal and communication skills:

Very good interpersonal and communications skills, including writing scientific manuscripts and delivery of oral presentations.

4) Relevant experience:

Experience in spectroscopy and quantum optics is highly desirable.
Experience in simulations and nanofabrication are desirable but not essential.

Appointment at Research Associate level is dependent on having a PhD. Those who have submitted but not yet received their PhD will be appointed at Research Assistant level, which will be amended to Research Associate once the PhD has been awarded.

 Starting salary from £26,707 per annum, dependent on skills and experience, with an annual increment up to £30,378 per annum.  

UEA has some of the most innovative and highly regarded centres for research in the UK. Applications are invited for the post of Research Technician in Evolutionary Genetics to assist in research under the supervision of Dr Karl Grieshop, working on a newly funded project that aims to understand the evolutionary repeatability of sex- and age-specific fitness in Drosophila. 

The aim of the project is to evaluate the genomic basis of sex- and age-specific fitness across ten Drosophila species to determine whether molecular evolution produces repeatable, predictable solutions to common adaptive challenges. The research uses a unique combination of Drosophila breeding designs, genomic resequencing, and bioinformatics. 

Key duties of the role include receiving, culturing, and maintaining laboratory populations across multiple Drosophila species, carrying out regular stock maintenance, scaling up population sizes, Drosophila husbandry, and population cage assays. Key duties also include sample collection, processing, DNA extractions, quality control, liaising with colleagues and support staff on day-to-day laboratory operations, contributing to lab meetings, research discussions, and related group projects. 

 You will have a graduate level qualification (BSc or equivalent qualification/experience) in biological sciences, genetics, molecular biology, zoology, or a related discipline. Essential requirements include practical skills in core molecular biology techniques (genomic DNA extraction, quantification, and quality control), experience with insect husbandry or handling laboratory organisms, strong organisational and problem-solving skills, meticulous attention to detail and record-keeping. Prior experience working specifically with Drosophila, familiarity with next-generation sequencing sample preparation (e.g., Illumina library workflows), or basic experience in command-line bioinformatics environments would be advantageous. 

 This full-time post is available from 1 February 2027 on a fixed term basis for three years.  

We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive. We particularly welcome applicants with the protected characteristic of disability, and race (Black, Asian and minority ethnic) for this post, as they are currently underrepresented in this type of role within the Faculty. Appointment will be made on merit and all applicants will be scored against the same criteria.

 Benefits include:

 34 days annual leave inclusive of Bank Holidays and University Customary days (pro rata for part-time). 

 Family and Work-life balance policies including hybrid working and considerable maternity, paternity, shared parental leave and adoption leave. 

 Generous pension scheme with life cover for dependants, plus incapacity cover. 

 Health and Wellbeing:  discounted access to Sportspark facilities, relaxation rooms, 320 acres of rolling parkland, wellbeing walks, Wellbeing Ambassador network, on-campus medical centre including NHS Dentist, Occupational Health and a 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme. 

 Campus Facilities: Sportspark, library, nursery, supermarket, post office, bars and catering outlets. 

 Exclusive shopping discounts to help cut the cost of household bills, childcare salary sacrifice scheme, Cycle to Work scheme and public transport discounts. 

 Personal Development: unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning courses, specialist advice and training from our Organisational Development and Professional Learning Team.

 Closing date: 30 November 2026 

The University holds an Athena Swan Silver Institutional Award in recognition of our advancement towards gender equality. 

 Further Information.

 For an informal discussion about the post please contact  Dr Karl Grieshop  via  K.Grieshop@uea.ac.uk .

 We are seeking a talented and motivated Research Associate in Sulfur Biology to join the Department of Molecular and Cell Biology, LISCB. This full-time, three-year fixed-term role offers an exciting opportunity to lead an interdisciplinary research project investigating how hypoxic Escherichia coli convert cystine into reactive sulfur species and elemental sulfur. You will take day-to-day ownership of the project, designing and delivering experiments that combine microbial physiology, genetics and chemically rigorous sulfur analysis, while working independently and collaboratively to achieve agreed research milestones.

 You will integrate microbiological, biochemical and chemical data to uncover the mechanisms and consequences of bacterial sulfur metabolism under low-oxygen conditions. Working with internal and external collaborators, you will contribute to specialist analytical approaches including GC-MS, LC-MS, NMR, Raman spectroscopy and electron microscopy, prepare high-quality publications and present findings at research meetings and conferences.  Applications are invited for a joint Oxford-SETI Institute Postdoctoral Research Fellowship in Planetary Climate. The Department of Physics invites applications for a prestigious independent fellowship in the broad area of Planetary Climate. This fellowship is funded jointly by the department and by the SETI Institute. The successful applicant will be based in the Astrophysics sub-department at Oxford, and will also be an active member of the SETI Institute’s vibrant cohort of postdoctoral fellows. They will also join the Oxford Planets and Life Initiative, where they are encouraged to make broader interdisciplinary scientific collaborations.

 The Fellow will lead a personal research programme in one or more subject areas relevant to exoplanets, planetary climate, and/or habitability. Research Fellow A / B in Advanced Signal Processing for Future Communications Systems

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. 

We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.  

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.  

The role

The Institute for Communication Systems (ICS) home of the 5G and 6G Innovation Centre (5GIC/6GIC) is looking to recruit a Research Fellow in Advanced Signal Processing for Future Communications Systems. The successful candidate will be part of the Wireless Systems Lab group and will have the opportunity to work very close with our industrial partners as well as with academic partners all over the world.

The research will focus on the design, analysis and evaluation of advanced transceiver processing algorithms. Topics include MIMO, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), low-complexity non-linear detection, channel coding, and PHY design for non-terrestrial networks (NTN). The role combines theoretical analysis with simulation-based and, where appropriate, experimental validation.

The successful candidate will publish in leading journals and conferences, contribute to grant proposals and intellectual property, and help supervise PhD students.

ICS is the largest academic research institute in Europe specialising in all aspects of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies). It is home to over 200 researchers with expertise in all communication and broadcasting systems and has developed the best in class large scale testbeds for research and innovation and enjoys the state-of-the-art lab and computing facilities.

Established in 2012, 5GIC is the world’s first dedicated centre in researching end-to-end aspects of 5G and works closely with national and international leading academic institutes and key industrial partners. In November 2020, 6GIC was officially launched with parallel research undertaken in both 5G+ and 6G for 2030+.

Please refer to the essential criteria in the Job Profiles for a Research Fellow A and B attached for further details.

Please note that these roles will be offered at either Research Fellow A or Research Fellow B level depending on your experience (see job profile below for further details). The salary range for a Research Fellow A starts at £38,448 and Research Fellow B starts at £48,337.

On the UK side, where the post will be based, the lead investigators are Nick Chater and Hossam Zeitoun in the Behavioural Science Group at Warwick Business School.

 

Over the past two years, the project team has carried out a broad programme of experimental and computational research investigating contractualist theories of moral reasoning, focusing primarily on human–human social interaction. The work has combined online behavioural experiments, game-theoretic paradigms, vignette studies and Bayesian computational modelling. The successful candidate will join the existing research team and contribute to the next phase of the project through experimental research, computational modelling, or both, depending on their expertise. The final stage of the project is also expected to explore the implications of this work for human–AI interaction.

 Cardiff University Brain Research Imaging Centre (CUBRIC), School of Psychology 

 We are seeking a Research Associate to join CUBRIC to work on the UKRI-funded project “Physics-Led Development of Brain Digital Twin Technology Using Low-Cost MRI and EEG in Sub-Saharan Africa”. The project is led by University College London in partnership with Cardiff University, Mbarara University of Science and Technology and Makerere University (Uganda), with partners at the University of Pavia, Aix-Marseille University and Leiden University.

 Brain digital twins – personalised computational models of brain dynamics built with platforms such as The Virtual Brain – currently depend on high-field MRI and high-density EEG, which are available only in a few well-resourced centres. This project aims to show that brain digital twins grounded in physics can be built from ultra-low-field MRI and portable EEG, and to build lasting research capacity in this field in Uganda.

 You will lead the Cardiff contribution to the development of physics-based acquisition protocols for ultra-low-field MRI, in particular diffusion-weighted imaging for reconstructing the structural connectome, working with the team in Mbarara, who operate a Halbach-array scanner. You will develop pipelines for tractography and structural connectivity from ultra-low-field data, benchmark them against high-field data, and work with colleagues at UCL, Pavia and Marseille to integrate the resulting connectomes into brain digital twin simulations. The role has a strong training component: you will contribute to an open online lecture series on the physics of brain digital twins and help deliver a School on the topic in Uganda, working closely with postdoctoral researchers there. The post involves international travel, including to Uganda.

 You will hold a PhD (or be close to submission) in physics, engineering, neuroscience or a related discipline, with experience of MRI acquisition and/or diffusion MRI analysis and strong programming skills. Experience of low-field MRI, EEG or whole-brain modelling would be an advantage.

 CUBRIC is one of Europe’s leading brain imaging centres, housing MRI systems ranging from portable ultra-low-field MRI to 3T scanners, including the ultra-strong-gradient Connectome scanner, alongside MEG, EEG and TMS facilities.

 For informal enquiries, please contact Professor Mara Cercignani ( cercignanim@cardiff.ac.uk ).

About the role

We invite applications for a 3-year postdoctoral position in the Computational Regulatory Genomics group at the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences (LMS) / Institute of Clinical Sciences. The successful candidate will play a central role in the analysis and interpretation of diverse omics data within the cis-ARC consortium that studies cis-regulatory mechanisms governing vertebrate development. It has been established that long-range promoter-enhancer interactions are indispensable for the normal transcription of key developmental regulatory genes, including transcription factors. These interactions occur within landscapes of extremely conserved noncoding elements – genomic regulatory blocks (GRBs). However, neither the source, nor the functional importance, of this extreme evolutionary conservation has been elucidated.

The successful applicant will perform statistical modelling and develop computational methods to analyse publicly available and consortium-generated omics data with the aim to provide mechanistic hypotheses about transcription regulation within GRBs during zebrafish development.

What you would be doing

You will perform whole-genome alignment and identification of conserved non-coding elements and their clusters in the zebrafish genome. Using statistical methods, you will integrate the sequence conservation signal, 3D-genome sequencing datasets and data on chromatin accessibility and gene expression to delineate genomic regulatory blocks, find regulated genes and predict their long-range interactions with cis-regulatory elements. Using the obtained comprehensive view of transcription regulation in selected GRBs in normal development, you will help prioritise regulatory loci for perturbations to observe and interpret emerging phenotypes. For this, you will be working closely with experimental groups of the cis-ARC consortium. You will also have an opportunity to collaborate with other members of the Computational Regulatory Genomics group.

What we are looking for

A PhD (or equivalent) in a relevant field of biology, such as computational biology, bioinformatics, molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry.
First author publication in relevant and refereed journals.
Experience and expertise in more than one of the following areas: analysis and interpretation of bulk or single-cell RNA sequencing or ATAC data, Hi-C-type data, ChIP-seq / CUT&RUN or similar data, CAGE-seq data.
Experience in at least one of the following areas: whole-genome alignment, single nucleotide polymorphism or indel calling and annotation, analysis of evolutionary sequence conservation.
Experience in the analysis or modelling of functional promoter-enhancer associations; or experience in statistical modelling or bioinformatics software/database development.
Excellent communication skills and experience of collaborative work within a research group.

What we can offer you

Opportunity to do cutting-edge research on a topic important for both fundamental and translational molecular biology
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity
Excellent opportunities for professional development through collaborations within and outside the group
Access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

This is a full-time, fixed term post for 3 years.

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant.

 About the role : 

 Supported by BBSRC funding, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join the group of Dr Rachel Lai at Imperial College London. 

 Macrophages are essential sentinels of innate immunity, but their dysregulated activation drives severe inflammatory diseases. Macrophage activation requires the convergence of biophysical and biochemical inputs, including acute metabolic shifts, ionic fluxes and oxidative stress. Working within a dynamic, multi-institutional team, you will employ biological and analytical assays and tools to define the physiological checkpoints that determine how macrophages integrate these stress signals and transition from homeostasis to a proinflammatory state. 

 What you would be doing : 

 You will lead studies investigating how metabolic and ionic shifts govern macrophage activation, taking responsibility for experimental planning and execution, data analysis and manuscript preparation.

 Working closely with members of the Lai group and collaborators across the multi-institutional team, you will develop and apply experimental approaches to deliver the project’s scientific aims.

 You will also supervise and train students, share expertise with colleagues and contribute to the day-to-day running of the laboratory.

 You will present findings at scientific conferences, prepare reports for research funders and contribute to future grant applications.

 A PhD in Immunology, Physiology, Cell Biology or a closely related discipline.

 *Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. 

 Practical experience with primary macrophages or relevant cell-culture models, with strong knowledge of innate immunity and macrophage biology.

 Experience studying immunometabolism or cellular physiology, including functional immunology and biochemical assays.

 Ability to lead independent research and work collaboratively, with experience in experimental planning, data analysis and scientific writing. 

 Experience in one or more of the following is highly desirable but not essential: measuring cellular ion fluxes or transporter/channel activity, mass spectrometry-based proteomics or metabolomics, bioinformatics or computational analysis of omics datasets, or working with small-animal models. Holding a relevant UK personal licence would also be advantageous.

About You

Applications are invited for the position of Post-Doctoral Research Associate in MRI Physics in the Research Department of Imaging Physics & Engineering, School of Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Sciences (BMEIS) at King’s College London.  

This position is based in central London at St Thomas’ Hospital. We work in a multi-disciplinary, closely integrated environment with a strong focus on developing new MRI acquisition and reconstruction techniques that can benefit patients, and state-of-the-art MRI facilities.

About The Role

This is an exciting opportunity for a talented and highly motivated researcher to join our lab and contribute to the development of MRI pulse sequences and AI-based reconstruction algorithms to improve prostate cancer diagnosis.

Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in UK men. While MRI plays a key role in the prostate cancer diagnostic pathway, it still requires further technical developments for a faster and more accurate diagnosis.

The post-doctoral research associate will develop improved and robust prostate MRI pulse sequences and AI-based reconstruction algorithms, optimise acquisition protocols, collect and analyse data, and integrate the developments inline on the scanner to facilitate clinical translation and support a clinical study in patients referred to our clinical service with suspected prostate cancer. A strong focus on this position will be 3D quantitative MRI techniques, including diffusion-weighted imaging. The post-doctoral research associate will publish their findings in the major journals and conferences of the field.

This is a full time post (37 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for two years.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: 

Essential criteria

PhD (or near completion) in Physics, Applied Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, or related field
Profound knowledge in MRI Physics, including pulse sequence development and AI-based image reconstruction
Good programming skills (Matlab, Python, C++)
Excellent scientific writing and presentation skills
Interest in clinical applications of MRI
Ability to work independently on a research problem
Collaborative approach within a research group

Previous experience with quantitative MRI

 This post is part-time 0.6 fte for a period of 12 months, ideally starting in December 2026 (or as soon as possible thereafter).

 The School of Sport, Nutrition and Allied Health Professionals is looking to appoint a suitably qualified individual as a Research Assistant to work with a project team based at Oxford Brookes University, University College London and Lund University, Sweden. You will be involved at the start of an exciting new project to adapt an evidence-based Occupational Therapy-specific intervention which was developed in Sweden and is widely used in their mental health services to the UK.

 The funded research project aims to work in collaboration with co-developers, occupational therapists and service users to:

 1) To explore, and identify in what ways the Balancing Everyday Life (BEL) intervention manual should be modified for delivery in the UK healthcare context.

 2) To elucidate and refine the Logic Model for the UK version of BEL manual.

 3) To conduct a preliminary evaluation of modifications with adults diagnosed with a mental health population and using mental health services and make required modifications to form the BEL UK version.

 4) To cross-culturally develop a UK English language version of the SDO-OB measure for use in mental health services in the UK.

 With the team, you will support the preparation for and co-delivering of focus groups with occupational therapists and service users. You will be involved in completing outcome measures with research participants and conducting one-to-one interviews. You will be involved in both quantitative and qualitative data analysis and preparing articles for publication.

 Applications are invited from individuals who have experience of mixed methods health or social care research, excellent communication and time-management skills, and must have completed.

 The ability to manage your own workload and to work as part of a team are essential.

 A good degree

 Excellent organisational skills

 We are currently inviting applications for two Postdoctoral Research Associate positions to work with Professors Jon Keating and James Maynard at the Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford. These are three-year, fixed-term positions, supported by a Simons Collaboration grant funded the Simons Foundation that commences in January 2027. The starting date of the positions is flexible, between January 2027 and October 2027. 

 The successful candidates will be part of an international collaboration carrying out research at the interface between number theory and probability theory, funded by a Simons Collaboration on Universal Statistics in Number Theory.  We are seeking an enthusiastic and ambitious Postdoctoral Research Fellow for a unique role, cross-cutting two interconnected and growing interdisciplinary programmes of research into Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD support for children and young people (CYP) with serious and complex mental health needs, (CYPIMHS) at the University of Salford. This new 12-month post provides an exciting opportunity to help shape the next stage of our research.

 Working with an established multi professional team, You will work across the FASD and CYPIMH research programme to develop the networks, strategic partnerships, knowledge mobilisation and impact required to translate individual projects into sustainable programmes of research. 

 You will provide strategic support to academic staff across a range of disciplines in gathering, evidencing and shaping impact case studies; strengthening knowledge-exchange activity with policy, practice, industry and communities; and maximising our responsiveness to external funding opportunities.

 Work collaboratively with academic leads to support the development of  research programmes and REF 2029 impact case studies across  Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) and support for children and young people with serious and complex mental health needs requiring intensive intervention (CYPIMHS). 

 Design and implement appropriate methods to gather evidence of research impact from external stakeholders, partners and beneficiaries. 

 Conduct both qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis (e.g. interviews, surveys, focus groups, documentary analysis). 

 Map pathways to impact in collaboration with researchers, identifying key evidence gaps and support needs.

 About the Faculty 

 The Centre for Applied Health Research at the University of Salford has a growing portfolio of interdisciplinary FASD and CYPIMHS research spanning complex intervention development and evaluation, population health, clinical research and criminal justice, health service delivery research, and co-production with young people and families, alongside emerging University investment in neuroimaging and biomarker research.  

 This is a unique opportunity to work with a multi-professional team, working at the cutting edge of two interconnected and exciting areas of health research.

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

The laboratory of Prof Chris Toseland (www.toseland-lab.com) invites applications to the position of a Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA) with skills in cell biophysics to work on an exciting project funded by the BBSRC. The interdisciplinary project aims to characterise the nuclear organisation of proteins regulating transcription in cancer cells.

 

To enhance chances of success on this project, we encourage applicants with prior knowledge of cell imaging, and single molecule imaging & analysis.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

 

Plan and deliver day-to-day research investigating the nuclear organisation of proteins involved in transcriptional regulation in cancer cells. Work with the Principal Investigator to establish experimental priorities, agree achievable milestones and manage progress within the fixed-term appointment.
Design and perform experiments to investigate the distribution, dynamics and interactions of transcription-associated proteins within the nucleus. Select appropriate experimental controls and replication, critically evaluate findings and use results to inform subsequent experiments.
Maintain and prepare mammalian cell cultures for imaging and biophysical experiments, ensuring consistent sample quality and following appropriate procedures for cell handling, experimental treatments and sample preparation.
Use advanced fluorescence microscopy, including live-cell, high-resolution and single-molecule imaging, to characterise nuclear protein organisation and behaviour. Optimise sample preparation and image acquisition conditions to obtain reliable, reproducible datasets.
Analyse imaging and single-molecule datasets using appropriate quantitative methods and software. Assess data quality, interpret measurements in their biological context and prepare clear figures and summaries that communicate the principal findings.
Contribute to complementary biophysical experiments, where required by the project, working with colleagues and collaborators using approaches such as atomic force microscopy and optical tweezers. Integrate these findings with imaging results to develop a broader understanding of nuclear organisation.
Identify and troubleshoot experimental and analytical problems, adapting established protocols where necessary. Exercise independent judgement within agreed project objectives and seek specialist advice when appropriate.
Maintain accurate, complete and accessible records of experimental procedures, results and analysis. Organise and store research data in accordance with University requirements and good research practice, enabling findings to be checked and work to be continued by other team members.
Communicate progress through regular discussions with the Principal Investigator, research group meetings and interactions with UK collaborators. Prepare presentations and concise progress summaries, highlighting findings, technical challenges and priorities for further work.
Take a leading role, in agreement with the Principal Investigator, in preparing figures, methods and results for manuscripts arising from the research. Critically assess relevant literature and use it to inform experimental design, interpretation and scientific writing.
Follow relevant health and safety procedures, contribute to risk assessments and use shared facilities and equipment responsibly. Undertake other duties appropriate to the grade and remit of the post.

Role Description

Department

The Faculty of Social Sciences at the University of York is making a strategic investment to enhance EU research income and support our academic departments in pursuing Horizon Europe and other major funding streams. 

The Faculty's end-to-end research support team provides unified operational service across pre-award, post-award, and research environment & development to enable high-impact, interdisciplinary research.

Role

The EU Research Coordinator will provide specialist support on EU research funding to enable academic staff in the Faculty of Social Sciences to develop and submit competitive funding applications. Focusing primarily on research development for new bids, particularly across Horizon Europe, the postholder will also manage the full pre-award process and ensure compliance with funder expectations. 

The key responsibilities include horizon scanning for funding opportunities, advising on proposal structure and non-technical content, coordinating consortiums, and managing pre-award costings and internal approvals. Additionally, the role holder will support the development of Faculty research themes and build shared resources to enhance EU research income and grant capture across departments.

Skills, Experience & Qualification needed

Knowledge of higher education research, including the funding landscape

Good knowledge of EU research funding programmes

Experience in supporting the development, preparation and submission of research funding applications, including for EU research funding

Excellent numeracy skills, competent working with complex project budgets, demonstrating accuracy and attention to detail

Able to effectively organise and prioritise work and follow procedures in order to produce work to a high standard to required deadlines

Proactive approach to solving complex problems, including resolving issues escalated from the team

Level 3 qualification (e.g., A levels) or equivalent professional experience.
